nausea.title: Nausea
nausea.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
nausea.why: Sartre's novel of a man losing his grip on reality; readers say it unsettled them, a first existentialist read.

berry pickers.title: The Berry Pickers
berry pickers.author: Amanda Peters
berry pickers.why: A girl is taken from a Mi'kmaq berry-picking family and raised elsewhere; readers say it is very good.

shards of honor.title: Shards of Honor
shards of honor.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
shards of honor.why: Bujold's first Vorkosigan novel, a romance between two officers from enemy worlds; the start of a loved series.

these violent delights.title: These Violent Delights
these violent delights.author: Micah Nemerever
these violent delights.why: An obsessive friendship between two teenage boys turns dangerous; a Hitchcock-style LGBTQ+ thriller readers devour.

witchcraft for wayward girls.title: Witchcraft for Wayward Girls
witchcraft for wayward girls.author: Grady Hendrix
witchcraft for wayward girls.why: Pregnant teen girls in a 1970s home discover real witchcraft; a gripping, feminist horror read.

day of the triffids.title: The Day of the Triffids
day of the triffids.author: John Wyndham
day of the triffids.why: Comments do not discuss this novel and seem to mention other books.

strangers.title: Strangers
strangers.author: Belle Burden
strangers.why: The comments discuss Koontz and Yamada novels with the same title; the entry does not match.

mercy of gods.title: The Mercy of Gods
mercy of gods.author: James S. A. Corey
mercy of gods.why: Humans are enslaved by an alien empire in the start of a new James S. A. Corey series; deserves more attention.

chaos.title: Chaos
chaos.author: Tom O'Neill
chaos.why: O'Neill's long investigation into the Manson murders and the official story; readers became obsessed with it.

once and future witches.title: The Once and Future Witches
once and future witches.author: Alix E. Harrow
once and future witches.why: Three sisters revive witchcraft in an alternate 1890s America; readers love the prose and feminist spirit.

fall on your knees.title: Fall on Your Knees
fall on your knees.author: Ann-Marie MacDonald
fall on your knees.why: A multigenerational Canadian family saga of secrets and tragedy; readers say its opening line stays with you.

water moon.title: Water Moon
water moon.author: Samantha Sotto Yambao
water moon.why: A whimsical, magical story with inventive worldbuilding; one reader's only five-star book in nearly two years.

satantango.title: Sátántangó
satantango.author: László Krasznahorkai
satantango.why: Krasznahorkai's long-sentence novel about a decaying Hungarian village and a charismatic con man; strange and demanding.

gregor the overlander.title: Gregor the Overlander
gregor the overlander.author: Suzanne Collins
gregor the overlander.why: A boy falls into an underground world full of giant creatures; a good, underrated read for kids and parents.

monk.title: The Monk
monk.author: Matthew Gregory Lewis
monk.why: A scandalous Gothic novel of a pious monk's downfall; readers found it lived up to expectations.

myth of sisyphus.title: The myth of Sisyphus
myth of sisyphus.author: Albert Camus
myth of sisyphus.why: Camus's essay on absurdity and how to live well anyway; a reader says it helped them through hard times.

butchers masquerade.title: The Butcher’s Masquerade
butchers masquerade.author: Matt Dinniman
butchers masquerade.why: The fourth Dungeon Crawler Carl novel, a gruesomely funny survival-game adventure that fans of the series eagerly read.

machine stops.title: The Machine Stops
machine stops.author: E. M. Forster
machine stops.why: Forster's short story of people living underground, entirely dependent on a machine; a prescient classic.

foucaults pendulum.title: Foucault's Pendulum
foucaults pendulum.author: Umberto Eco
foucaults pendulum.why: Eco's novel about editors who invent a conspiracy that comes true; spans two millennia of secret societies.

new york.title: New York
new york.author: Edward Rutherfurd
new york.why: Rutherfurd takes you through three centuries of New York's history by following families; very long but enjoyable.

physician.title: The Physician
physician.author: Noah Gordon
physician.why: A boy in medieval England travels to Persia to learn medicine; readers say it is as good as The Pillars of the Earth.

book of doors.title: The Book of Doors
book of doors.author: Gareth Brown
book of doors.why: A bookseller finds a book that can open doors anywhere; a fun fantasy suggested as a light read.

seven moons of maali almeida.title: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
seven moons of maali almeida.author: Shehan Karunatilaka
seven moons of maali almeida.why: A dead photographer in the afterlife solves his own murder amid Sri Lanka's civil war; a Booker winner.

penpal.title: Penpal
penpal.author: Dathan Auerbach
penpal.why: Linked creepypasta-style tales of childhood stalking; readers say it gave them chills.

another country.title: Another Country
another country.author: James Baldwin
another country.why: Baldwin's novel of race, sexuality and friendship in 1950s New York; readers find it powerful and beautiful.

recognitions.title: The Recognitions
recognitions.author: William Gaddis
recognitions.why: Gaddis's huge, difficult novel about art forgery and authenticity; admirers call it a masterpiece.

pandoras star.title: Pandora's Star
pandoras star.author: Peter F. Hamilton
pandoras star.why: A wide-ranging space opera of wormhole travel and alien threat; readers like its scale though not all of its detail.

vicious.title: Vicious
vicious.author: V. E. Schwab
vicious.why: Two former friends become enemies with superpowers; recommended as a dark, fast take on the superhero story.

words of radiance.title: Words of Radiance
words of radiance.author: Brandon Sanderson
words of radiance.why: One reader calls it a slog; no clear recommendation here.

knight and the moth.title: The Knight and the Moth
knight and the moth.author: Rachel Gillig
knight and the moth.why: A knight seeks to restore a wizard-ruled realm in a book readers find unique and well-executed.

daughter of the forest.title: Daughter of the Forest
daughter of the forest.author: Juliet Marillier
daughter of the forest.why: A girl must spin shirts of nettles to free her brothers in this Irish retelling of The Wild Swans; deeply loved.

all the ugly and wonderful things.title: All the ugly and wonderful things
all the ugly and wonderful things.author: Bryn Greenwood
all the ugly and wonderful things.why: A young girl and a much older man form a troubling bond; a difficult, uncomfortable book that stays with readers.

hyperbole and a half.title: Hyperbole and a Half
hyperbole and a half.author: Allie Brosh
hyperbole and a half.why: Allie Brosh's illustrated essays on depression and daily chaos, funny enough to cheer up a dying relative.

deed of paksenarrion.title: The Deed of Paksenarrion
deed of paksenarrion.author: Elizabeth Moon
deed of paksenarrion.why: A farm girl becomes a soldier and paladin in a realistic fantasy series; a reader's most re-read book.

black leopard red wolf.title: Black Leopard, Red Wolf
black leopard red wolf.author: Marlon James
black leopard red wolf.why: Comments split sharply, with one reader unable to stand it; not clearly recommended.

ghost map.title: The Ghost Map
ghost map.author: Steven Johnson
ghost map.why: The 1854 London cholera outbreak and how a doctor and a priest traced it; a gripping blend of history and science.

bewilderment.title: Bewilderment
bewilderment.author: Richard Powers
bewilderment.why: The only mention is of a half-finished read with doubts; no clear recommendation.

sense and sensibility.title: Sense and Sensibility
sense and sensibility.author: Jane Austen
sense and sensibility.why: Austen's novel of two sisters who find love and sense in Regency England; a recommended classic.

cyberiad.title: The Cyberiad
cyberiad.author: Stanisław Lem
cyberiad.why: Lem's witty fables about two robot inventors; one reader says it is the hardest they have ever laughed.

all clear.title: Blackout / All Clear
all clear.author: Connie Willis
all clear.why: Historians in WWII-era England cannot get home in this time-travel pair; readers say it is a favourite.

little stranger.title: The Little Stranger
little stranger.author: Sarah Waters
little stranger.why: A doctor is drawn into a decaying country house haunted by something; a slow Gothic read for spooky season.

good soldier.title: The Good Soldier
good soldier.author: Ford Madox Ford
good soldier.why: Ford's tale of two couples and an unreliable narrator; praised as a masterpiece of deception.

certain hunger.title: A Certain Hunger
certain hunger.author: Chelsea G. Summers
certain hunger.why: A food critic narrates how she kills her lovers and cooks them; graphic enough to warn people with weak stomachs.

money.title: Money
money.author: Martin Amis
money.why: Amis's brash, satirical novel of a debauched ad man in 1980s London; praised for its stylish prose.

time travelers wife.title: The Time Traveler's Wife
time travelers wife.author: Audrey Niffenegger
time travelers wife.why: A man involuntarily time travels and loves a woman across his jumps; a romantic favourite.

ducks newburyport.title: Ducks, Newburyport
ducks newburyport.author: Lucy Ellmann
ducks newburyport.why: A thousand-page stream of thoughts of an Ohio housewife; readers find it hard going but admirably ambitious.

beauty.title: Beauty
beauty.author: Robin McKinley
beauty.why: McKinley's gentle retelling of Beauty and the Beast; recommended as a cosy fairytale.

white fang.title: White Fang
white fang.author: Jack London
white fang.why: A wild wolf-dog's life in the Yukon and beyond; Jack London's classic of survival.

algebraist.title: The Algebraist
algebraist.author: Iain Banks
algebraist.why: Banks's space opera of a slow-living alien species and a coming war; readers praise his writing.

shutter island.title: Shutter Island
shutter island.author: Dennis Lehane
shutter island.why: A US marshal investigates a patient's disappearance from an island asylum; a one-sitting thriller.

trinity.title: Trinity
trinity.author: Leon Uris
trinity.why: Uris's saga of Ireland's struggle through the lives of Catholic and Protestant families; a favourite of historical epics.

thousand acres.title: A Thousand Acres
thousand acres.author: Jane Smiley
thousand acres.why: King Lear on a farm in Iowa, showing a family tearing itself apart; praised and widely cited as a favourite.

revolutionary road.title: Revolutionary road
revolutionary road.author: Richard Yates
revolutionary road.why: A suburban couple's marriage crumbles in 1950s Connecticut; a bleak, powerful classic.

gargoyle.title: The gargoyle
gargoyle.author: Andrew Davidson
gargoyle.why: A burned man falls for a sculptor who claims to have known him in past lives; one reader's favourite.

briar club.title: The Briar Club
briar club.author: Kate Quinn
briar club.why: Women in a Washington boarding house in the 1950s keep secrets; readers love Quinn's work.

raven tower.title: The Raven Tower
raven tower.author: Ann Leckie
raven tower.why: A god narrates a story of a kingdom and its ruler; praised for its unusual narrator.

american war.title: American War
american war.author: Omar El Akkad
american war.why: A near-future second American civil war seen through one girl's life; grim, gripping and widely recommended.

starling house.title: Starling House
starling house.author: Alix E. Harrow
starling house.why: A young woman in Kentucky is drawn to a haunted house; enrapturing for readers who finished it in two days.

last exit to brooklyn.title: Last Exit to Brooklyn
last exit to brooklyn.author: Hubert Selby, Jr.
last exit to brooklyn.why: Selby's raw, shocking stories of Brooklyn's underworld; recommended as completely extreme.

hamlet.title: Hamlet
hamlet.author: William Shakespeare
hamlet.why: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Danish prince and his revenge; the quintessential play.

life impossible.title: The Life Impossible
life impossible.author: Matt Haig
life impossible.why: Reader calls it boring and predictable; not recommended.

survivor.title: Survivor
survivor.author: Chuck Palahniuk
survivor.why: Palahniuk's satirical novel narrated by the last member of a suicide cult; a reader found it gripping.

night watchman.title: The Night Watchman
night watchman.author: Louise Erdrich
night watchman.why: Erdrich's novel based on her grandfather fighting a 1950s bill to end Native tribes; vivid characters and a Pulitzer winner.

cruddy.title: Cruddy
cruddy.author: Lynda Barry
cruddy.why: Lynda Barry's illustrated novel is a dark, shocking story of a girl on the run; readers call it utterly wild.

brain on fire.title: Brain on fire
brain on fire.author: Susannah Cahalan
brain on fire.why: A young journalist's rare autoimmune disease nearly destroys her mind; a gripping medical memoir.

golden son.title: Golden Son
golden son.author: Pierce Brown
golden son.why: The second Red Rising book escalates the war between castes; a favourite of action-lovers.

christine.title: Christine
christine.author: Stephen King
christine.why: A boy becomes obsessed with a possessed 1958 Plymouth; one reader's favourite King.

calculating stars.title: The Calculating Stars
calculating stars.author: Mary Robinette Kowal
calculating stars.why: An alternate-history space race in the 1950s after a meteor strike, with a female mathematician at the centre.

man who mistook his wife for a hat.title: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
man who mistook his wife for a hat.author: Oliver Sacks
man who mistook his wife for a hat.why: Sacks's case histories of patients with strange neurological conditions; readers call it fascinating.

number the stars.title: Number the Stars
number the stars.author: Lois Lowry
number the stars.why: A Danish girl helps her Jewish friend escape the Nazis in 1943; a school favourite readers think about for years.
